title: Your First Weekend at University of Northern Iowa, Shared as Cards
description: An under-21-safe first-weekend sequence using campus landmarks, spaces, and nearby public recreation.

cards.title: Start with the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark walk
cards.notes: Begin with a daylight walk to the Campanile and take a few orientation photos before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable starting point for getting your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI’s archives document the Campanile as a campus memorial project begun in 1914 and built after years of planning.
cards.access_notes: Visit exterior campus grounds in daylight and follow posted university access guidance.

cards.title: Settle into Rod Library
cards.subtitle: Study rooms and campus resources
cards.notes: Use the library’s space information to choose a study room or a small-group meeting room that fits your plans.
cards.short_summary: A practical pause for studying, planning, or meeting up.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library offers study rooms for one to six people and meeting rooms for small to medium groups.
cards.access_notes: Room availability and reservations vary; consult the library’s room-selection links before relying on a particular room.

cards.title: Find the Union’s gathering spaces
cards.subtitle: Dining, events, and social space
cards.notes: Walk through the Coffeehouse and posted event areas, then check the Union calendar or student-involvement office for options.
cards.short_summary: A central campus stop for services, food, and event information.
cards.evidence_claim: Maucker Union has a central Coffeehouse, meeting rooms, a ballroom, dining options, and hosts thousands of events annually.
cards.source_title: Welcome, Mission & History | Student Involvement & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Public areas and services vary by time and event; check the Union directly for current access.

cards.entity_name: University of Northern Iowa Gallery of Art
cards.title: Take in the Gallery of Art
cards.subtitle: Kamerick Art Building
cards.notes: Add a self-guided gallery visit during academic-year hours, and use the displayed exhibition information to slow down and look closely.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission art stop inside Kamerick Art Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNI Gallery of Art is on the ground floor of Kamerick Art Building, and all of its programming is admission-free.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | University of Northern Iowa Gallery of Art
cards.access_notes: The gallery lists academic-year hours as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with break closures; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Check TheatreUNI’s next curtain time
cards.subtitle: Campus theatre venue
cards.notes: Look for an upcoming TheatreUNI production and make a plan with friends; use the official ticket office for event-specific details.
cards.short_summary: A campus venue for student-produced mainstage and smaller performances.
cards.evidence_claim: TheatreUNI presents four mainstage productions each season plus smaller performances at Strayer-Wood Theatre, with free tickets for current students.
cards.source_title: The Arts | University of Northern Iowa
cards.access_notes: Performance dates and ticket availability vary; consult the official event listing before going.

cards.title: Look ahead at Gallagher Bluedorn
cards.subtitle: Concerts, shows, and cultural events
cards.notes: Browse the official calendar for a show that fits your weekend, then confirm whether it is free, ticketed, or requires advance pickup.
cards.short_summary: A major campus arts venue with varied programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Gallagher Bluedorn hosts more than 400 events each year, including concerts, cultural shows, comedy, and Broadway musicals.
cards.source_title: The Arts | University of Northern Iowa
cards.access_notes: Event admission and schedules vary; use the venue’s official calendar or UNItix for the specific event.

cards.title: See the McLeod Center
cards.subtitle: Panther court-sports venue
cards.notes: Check the athletics schedule for a basketball, volleyball, or wrestling event, and confirm ticket requirements before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A named campus arena for multiple UNI athletics programs.
cards.evidence_claim: McLeod Center opened in 2006 and is the competition venue for UNI volleyball, basketball, and wrestling.
cards.access_notes: Entry is event-dependent; review the official schedule and ticket guidance for a particular game or event.

cards.title: Walk over to the UNI-Dome
cards.subtitle: Multipurpose stadium complex
cards.notes: Use the event calendar to see whether a game, tournament, or other public event lines up with your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A signature campus stadium used for athletics and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNI-Dome is a multipurpose stadium used for wrestling tournaments, track and field, softball, and football.
cards.access_notes: Public entry depends on scheduled activity and ticketing; confirm with the official event calendar.

cards.title: Scope out recreation options
cards.subtitle: Jacobson Human Performance Complex
cards.notes: Review Recreation Services offerings with a friend and confirm the membership or program requirement before planning an activity.
cards.short_summary: A recreation stop beside UNI’s major athletic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies the Wellness and Recreation Center as part of the Jacobson Human Performance Complex; some facilities require WRC membership.
cards.access_notes: The facilities page labels several amenities as requiring WRC membership; check current eligibility and program details first.

cards.title: Close with a Big Woods Lake lap
cards.subtitle: Cedar Falls public recreation area
cards.notes: If you have transportation and daylight, walk the paved lake loop or use the public trail connection for a low-key outdoor finish.
cards.short_summary: A nearby city recreation area with a paved loop around the lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Woods Lake Recreation Area has trail access to a 1.7-mile paved trail surrounding the lake, plus a kayak launch and disc golf course.
cards.source_title: Big Woods Lake Recreation Area | City of Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: Use daylight and follow City of Cedar Falls park rules; the city notes that shelters can be reserved in advance.
